title: Continuous session-preserving diversion for active-active gateway migrations
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: Our hosted API gateways need an active-active failover capability that preserves in-flight streaming sessions and conversational context while shifting traffic between regions. Prior incidents showed token loss and long-tail latency spikes during regional drains. Goal: implement a session-preserving diversion mechanism that meets SLOs (99.9% availability for request/response paths, 99% continuity for streaming handoffs within a 5s window), integrates with existing circuit breakers and load-shedding policies, and degrades gracefully under overload.
acceptance_criteria: Graceful diversion preserves KV cache and prefix tokens for >= 99% of streaming sessions during region-to-region shift
Failover path does not violate per-route P99 latency SLO by more than 10% in steady-state tests
Circuit-breaker policies trigger and shed low-priority traffic without interrupting pinned streaming sessions
Automated canary cutover completes with measurable telemetry and rollback hook in < 15 minutes
Runbook updated and on-call run through completed with < 1h mean-time-to-recover for simulated partial-region outage
implementation_notes: Approach: introduce a diversion controller that orchestrates live session handoff using a three-phase protocol: prepare (checkpoint KV/prefix), divert (start duplicating outbound requests to target region with sticky routing), settle (confirm target has warm state and confirm primary drain)
Use existing KV sync snapshot API from ENG-14257 for checkpoint/restore; add ephemeral token-preservation layer to store last-100 tokens per session encrypted in transit

Streaming considerations: adopt half-closed streaming handoff — primary forwards buffered tokens while target accepts new frames once its KV cache warms to threshold X (configurable); this avoids abrupt resets
Circuit-breaker integration: diversion controller queries per-region CB state; if target region is over-threshold, diversion is deferred and fallback uses degraded route with rate-limited replays
Load-shedding policy: define tiers (essential, interactive, background) and protect 'essential' streaming sessions from shedding unless severity == critical
Telemetry: emit diversion duration, percent-preserved tokens, timestamped events for prepare/divert/settle, and per-session continuity tags for tracing
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag gated. Internal staging with synthetic streaming clients reproducing production traffic patterns.
Stage 1: Canary small percentage (1%) of user traffic between two low-traffic regions with real sessions. Monitor diversion metrics for 24h.
Stage 2: Incremental expansion (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with automated health checks gating progress. Each step requires green SLO checks for 30m.
Stage 3: Default active-active diversion for cross-region drains, with automated rollback on sustained SLO violation or diversion error rate > 0.5%
Rollback: immediate flap to simple redirect-based failover and rehydrate primary with latest KV snapshot; notify on-call and abort canary if P99 latency increases > 20%
test_plan: Unit tests: diversion controller state transitions, CB gating logic, token snapshot/replay correctness
Integration tests: end-to-end with proxy, runtime, and KV-sync in staging region pair using scripted streaming clients
Performance tests: steady-state and spike ramp tests with 200k concurrent short-lived streaming sessions; measure P50/P95/P99 latency, and preserved-token ratio
Chaos experiments: kill 1 region's proxy plane mid-diversion, verify target resumes with <= 5s token gap for 95% of sessions
Security tests: verify ephemeral token encryption and KMS handshake during checkpoint replication
telemetry_queries: BigQuery: SELECT COUNTIF(preserved_tokens_ratio < 0.9)/COUNT(*) as failure_rate FROM diversion.sessions WHERE timestamp BETWEEN ...
Tracing: span filter: trace.tag('diversion.phase') to visualize prepare->divert->settle latencies
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV sync lag causes target to accept without full prefix -> mitigation: require warm threshold and soft-stall client until warm or fallback to mirrored forwarding
Risk: Increased tail latency during warmup -> mitigation: ramp diversion slowly, enable transient backpressure and drop background traffic first
Risk: Secret/token replication surface -> mitigation: ephemeral encryption keys per diversion and short TTLs, KMS audit turned on
Risk: Circuit-breaker thrashing between regions -> mitigation: add hysteresis timeout and require sustained healthy metric window before toggling routing
decisions: Will use three-phase prepare/divert/settle protocol instead of immediate cutover to avoid token loss
Essential sessions will be pinned to higher preservation priority and exempt from early load-shedding
Diversion controller will be implemented in edge-proxy control plane as library to allow reuse across hosted and dedicated environments
open_questions: What exact warm-threshold value for KV cache gives best tradeoff between latency and preservation? (A/B test candidates: 60%, 75%, 90%)
Do we need cross-region persistent session storage for long-running sessions (> 24h) or is ephemeral checkpointing sufficient?
Should diversion metrics be exposed to customers via Console or remain internal for first 90 days?
